authorities.rule: Routes own production path, intent, required primary components, and any route-level state set.
Do not copy route state arrays into Page contracts; Pages remain composition metadata.
Pages own route-keyed metadata and Block composition without redefining route intent or runtime states.
Blocks own reusable component membership plus responsive, theme, and accessibility composition expectations.
Components own normalized model, canonical action, canonical state, kind, and per-component agent guidance.
Runtime state IDs and recovery semantics come from the canonical state taxonomy; agents do not invent synonyms.
Interaction physics, token roles, reduced-motion behavior, forced-colors behavior, and exceptions come from the v1.3 interaction authority.
Normalized Commerce models and capability boundaries outrank provider payload shapes.
Mutations use canonical Commerce action names and dispatch semantics; agents do not invent provider verbs.
Reference product, license, price, lifecycle, and capability content may be rendered but must not be fabricated.

prohibitions.description: Do not change Commerce component or runtime contracts merely to mirror a provider payload.
Do not invent mutation names when a canonical Commerce action exists.
Do not invent state synonyms when the canonical state taxonomy defines the meaning.
Do not add route runtime state arrays to storefront/pages.json.
Do not create a second interaction taxonomy outside storefront/interactions.json.
Do not infer optional behavior from provider identity; read normalized capability flags.
Do not fabricate price, tax, reviews, guarantees, invoices, ownership history, license scope, entitlement, or subscription outcomes.
